structuredContent.governing_intent: Create a single reviewable CANDIDATE design document for the Pre-Python gate covering verifier independence, assurance policy, capability/authority including live deployment authority, and optional sandbox/container policy, using the supplied authority/evidence without implementing or approving architecture.
structuredContent.summary: The work packet is a bounded documentation-only design task with clear artifact path, explicit exclusions, named source authority, candidate status, acceptance rows G10-G12, and observable completion criteria. It is cohesive because the topics are materially coupled around BIU authority, assurance, verifier independence, and sandbox controls, and the output is one reviewable candidate artifact rather than separable implementation changes.
implementation_unknowns: Exact repository layout and whether the target candidate packet/readiness receipt directories already exist must be discovered during implementation.
The author must locate and cite the named local baseline/source documents and map their sections accurately without importing unstated decisions.
The document checker or local validation mechanism for path/coverage may need to be identified from existing project conventions.
The existing style and structure of neighboring Pre-Python architecture documents may need to be inspected for formatting consistency while avoiding implicit adoption of their unresolved choices.
structuredContent.verification_assessment: Acceptance is observable through review of the produced document and local packet/readiness evidence: it must define the specified constraints and contract semantics, include successful and failing examples, map claims to source/invariants, label proposed material semantics as CANDIDATE, record unresolved Founder decisions rather than inventing them, and avoid source/test/config/runtime changes. One independent content review can give a meaningful verdict against G10-G12 and the supplied authority because the work product is a bounded document with traceable criteria, not a live implementation.
material_risks: The author could accidentally convert candidate design text into asserted Founder-approved architecture rather than preserving CANDIDATE status.
The author could over-invent semantics beyond the cited authority instead of presenting options/tradeoffs and unresolved Founder decisions.
Cross-document dependencies may tempt implicit adoption of neighboring candidate decisions that the packet explicitly says must not be adopted implicitly.
Security-sensitive topics such as capabilities, live deployment authority, credentials, and sandbox fallback require careful wording to avoid weakening trust boundaries.
The task allows only documentation and local packet/readiness evidence changes, so any source, config, service, secret, runtime, or public publication change would be out of scope.
structuredContent.next_action: Proceed to draft the candidate design artifact and any authorized local packet/readiness evidence, then perform an independent document-focused review against G10-G12, source mappings, scope exclusions, and candidate-status requirements.
structuredContent.rationale: READY is controlled by the presence of clear governing intent, bounded authorized outputs, resolved authority for documentation-only work, cohesive subject matter, explicit exclusions, and reviewable acceptance criteria. Remaining uncertainty is implementation research about locating and mapping existing sources and applying local documentation conventions, not unresolved owner intent. The three acceptance rows are related parts of one capability-and-assurance model, so splitting would create artificial boundaries and reduce coherence. No supplied evidence establishes a missing prerequisite or conflicting repository ownership that would require HOLD.
